read.sections.0.heading.source: A question, a proposal and a project
read.sections.0.heading.back: A question, a proposal and a project

read.sections.0.text.source: In 1950, a British scientist called Alan Turing asked, “Can machines think?” Computers were new, huge and slow. On 31 August 1955, four researchers in the United States wrote a proposal for a summer study of “artificial intelligence”. They believed every part of learning could be described well enough for a machine to copy it. The proposal was a plan. The project itself took place at Dartmouth College in 1956. AI is one part of digital technology. It needs computers to run, and later it also used networks and digital data.
read.sections.0.text.back: In 1950, a British scientist named Alan Turing asked, “Can machines think?” Computers at that time were new, very big and slow. On 31 August 1955, four researchers in the United States wrote a proposal for a summer study about “artificial intelligence” (kecerdasan buatan). They believed every part of learning could be described well enough for a machine to copy it. The proposal was a plan. The project itself took place at Dartmouth College in 1956. AI is one part of digital technology. It needs computers to run, and later it also used networks and digital data.

Later, it also used networks and data.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: In 1950, a British scientist, Alan Turing, asked: can machines think? On 31 August 1955, four researchers wrote a plan. read.sections.1.heading.source: Different ideas, big promises and AI winters
read.sections.1.heading.back: Different ideas, big promises and AI winters

read.sections.1.text.source: Researchers tried different ideas at the same time. Some wrote rules for computers to follow. Others built machines that learn from examples, like the perceptron in 1958. Much of the money came from governments. Some researchers made big promises, but real problems were harder than expected. Computers were slow, and there was little data. In 1973, a British report criticised much AI research, and Britain then cut funding for some of it. In the 1980s, companies used expert systems, built from rules that experts gave. They cost a lot to keep up, and their market fell in the late 1980s. Times like the mid-1970s and the late 1980s are called AI winters. Historians still argue about their exact dates and causes.
read.sections.1.text.back: Researchers tried different ideas at the same time. Some wrote rules for computers to follow. Others built machines that learn from examples, like the perceptron in 1958. A lot of money came from governments. Some researchers made big promises, but real problems were harder than expected. Computers were slow, and there was very little data. In 1973, a British report criticised much AI research, and Britain then cut funding for some of it. In the 1980s, companies used expert systems, built from rules given by experts. These systems cost a lot to maintain, and their market declined in the late 1980s. Times like the mid-1970s and the late 1980s are called AI winters. Historians still debate their exact dates and causes.
read.sections.1.text.note: "AI winter" is "musim sejuk AI", a calque; Malaysia has no winter, but the lesson explains the term and the quick check asks what it means.

In the 1980s, firms used rules from experts. These cost a lot to keep up. In the late 1980s, their market fell. These slow times are called AI winters. People still argue about their dates and causes.

read.sections.2.text.source: There were successes too. In 1997, a chess computer called Deep Blue beat the world champion, Garry Kasparov, though it could only play chess. Machine learning, which began in the 1950s, grew much stronger after 2010. The internet gave researchers huge sets of labelled photos, and chips made for computer graphics made the work faster. In 2012, a university team built a program that was much better at naming things in photos. Today, teams in many places build AI, including in Southeast Asia, as Lesson 7 shows. AI developed through overlapping ideas, shaped by money, hope, computers and data.

watch.summary.source: In this video, a host called Jabril and a robot called John Green Bot talk about AI. AI is already part of daily life. It suggests videos, finishes words as you type, and helps decide some things about money and jobs. People have hopes and fears about it. The video links the name artificial intelligence to a summer project at Dartmouth College in 1956. The scientists there were very hopeful. Some said machines would soon be as clever as people. But they did not know how much data and computer power AI needs. So for a long time, progress was slow. This is called an AI winter. Then computers became much faster, and the internet made huge amounts of data. That is a big reason AI has grown so fast.
watch.summary.back: In this video, a host named Jabril and a robot named John Green Bot talk about AI. AI is already part of daily life. It suggests videos, finishes words as you type, and helps make some decisions about money and jobs. People have hopes and worries about it. This video links the name artificial intelligence (kecerdasan buatan) to the summer project at Dartmouth College in 1956. The scientists there were very hopeful. Some said machines would soon be as clever as people. But they did not know how much data and computer power AI needs. So for a long time, progress was slow. This is called an AI winter. Then computers became much faster, and the internet produced very large amounts of data. That is one big reason AI has grown so quickly.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: Turing's life outside this paper (his wartime work and how he was treated later) is told in films and books, and some learners may know of it. This lesson leaves it out. If it comes up, keep it brief and factual, and don't ask learners about anyone's personal life.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: Turing's life outside this paper (his work during the war and how he was treated later) is told in films and books, and some learners may know about it. This lesson does not touch on it. If it comes up, tell it briefly and based on facts, and do not ask learners about anyone's private life.

educatorNotes.0.source: For teachers who want more: much early US funding came through DARPA, a military research agency (Toosi and others). The Lighthill report was submitted in March 1972 and published in 1973; it is often said to have caused Britain's first AI winter, but Agar (2020) shows the Science Research Council then funded some kinds of AI and not others. Haigh (2024) argues the deeper winter came in the late 1980s, after the expert-systems boom. The evidence (the proposal card and the timeline) is real; the Tomorrow Today headlines in the activity are made up, though each one matches a real period.
educatorNotes.0.back: For teachers who want to know more: much early funding in the United States came through DARPA, a military research agency (Toosi and colleagues). The Lighthill report was submitted in March 1972 and published in 1973; it is often said to have caused Britain's first AI winter, but Agar (2020) shows that the Science Research Council then funded some kinds of AI and not other kinds. Haigh (2024) argues that the worse winter came in the late 1980s, after the expert-systems boom. The evidence (the proposal card and the timeline) is real; the Tomorrow Today headlines in this activity are invented, though each one matches a real period.

educatorNotes.1.source: Paper version of the activity: write the eight headlines on cards and sort them into “A big promise”, “A careful claim” and “Hard to say”. There is no score; reward reasons, especially pointing to words like “soon”, “every” and “may”.
educatorNotes.1.back: Paper version of this activity: write the eight headlines on cards and sort them into “A big promise”, “A careful claim” and “Hard to say”. There are no marks; value the reasons given, especially when learners point to words like “soon”, “every” and “may”.
